exp: All the deals a sales rep is currently working on.
ex: Our Q4 pipeline shows $2M in qualified opportunities.
ex2: I'll add this account to my pipeline after the discovery call.
tip: Accent sur la 1re syllabe : PIPE-lyne, pas pi-pe-LINE.
err: Ne dites pas « le pipe » seul ; toujours « pipeline ».
mem: Imaginez les deals coulant dans un tuyau vers le revenu.

exp: A prediction of how much revenue will close in a given period.
ex: My forecast for this quarter is 1.4 million in committed deals.
ex2: Sales leadership reviews the forecast every Monday morning.
tip: « FOR-cast », pas « for-CAST ». Le 'a' est court.
err: Évitez « forecast of sales » : dites simplement « sales forecast ».
mem: Fore (avant) + cast (lancer) = lancer un chiffre à l'avance.

exp: A revenue target a salesperson must hit, usually quarterly.
ex: She crushed her quota last quarter — 130% to plan.
ex2: If we close this enterprise deal, the whole team hits quota.
err: « My quota of » est rare ; on dit « hit / miss / blow past quota ».
mem: Quota → quote → un chiffre que tu dois citer chaque trimestre.

exp: When customers cancel or stop paying for the product.
ex: Reducing churn is our top priority for the next two quarters.
ex2: A 5% monthly churn rate compounds quickly and severely erodes ARR.
tip: Son « tch » initial comme dans « church ». Évitez « shurn ».
err: « Churn out » signifie produire en masse, pas perdre des clients.
mem: Penser à la baratte (churn) qui agite le lait : agitation = clients qui partent.

exp: When a customer extends their contract for another term.
ex: The renewal conversation should start 90 days before the contract ends.
ex2: Auto-renewal clauses make life easier for both sides.
tip: « ri-NOO-ul » (3 syllabes). Le 'w' est presque muet.
err: Pas « renewment » (n'existe pas). Toujours « renewal ».
mem: Re + new = rendre à nouveau neuf le contrat.

exp: To sell a more expensive version of what the customer already has.
ex: We identified a clear upsell opportunity to the enterprise tier.
ex2: Upselling existing accounts is 5x cheaper than acquiring new logos.
tip: Stress sur UP. 'u' court comme dans « cup ».
err: Ne confondez pas avec « cross-sell » (produit différent).
mem: UP = monter en gamme, SELL = vendre.

exp: To sell a different product to the same customer.
ex: Cross-selling our security module added 30K ARR per account.
ex2: Strong cross-sell motion is what turns a product into a platform.
tip: Liaison fluide : « kross-sell », un seul mot.
err: Pas « cross-selling to the same product » : c'est UN AUTRE produit.
mem: CROSS = croiser des produits différents chez le même client.

exp: Annual Recurring Revenue — yearly subscription value.
ex: We closed 500K in net new ARR this quarter.
ex2: Investors care more about ARR growth than total revenue.
tip: On épelle lettre par lettre : « EY-AR-AR ».
err: ARR s'emploie souvent sans article : « ARR grew 20% ». Avec un nom comptable, on peut dire « an ARR target ».
mem: A = Annual, R = Recurring, R = Revenue.

exp: Monthly Recurring Revenue — predictable monthly subscription income.
ex: MRR grew 18% month over month — best in our history.
ex2: Track new MRR, expansion MRR, and churned MRR separately.
tip: « EM-AR-AR ». Bien marquer le M initial.
err: MRR × 12 ≠ ARR exact, à cause des annualisations ponctuelles.
mem: M comme Monthly. La sœur cadette d'ARR.

exp: Net Revenue Retention — how much revenue you keep and grow from existing customers.
ex: Our NRR sits at 118%, which means existing accounts are expanding.
ex2: Best-in-class SaaS companies report NRR above 120%.
err: NRR > 100% inclut l'expansion ; GRR ne l'inclut pas.
mem: NET = ce qui reste après churn ET expansion.

exp: Annual Contract Value — yearly value of a single contract.
ex: The average ACV for our enterprise segment is 95K.
ex2: Upmarket motion increased our average ACV by 60% in one year.
err: ACV ≠ ARR : ACV est par contrat, ARR est l'agrégat de tous.
mem: A = Annual, C = Contract, V = Value.

exp: Customer Acquisition Cost — what you spend to win one new customer.
ex: Our blended CAC dropped 22% after we cut paid spend.
ex2: The LTV-to-CAC ratio should be at least 3 to 1.
err: Inclure SDR, AE, marketing — pas seulement le paid media.
mem: C = Customer, A = Acquisition, C = Cost.

exp: Lifetime Value — total revenue a customer generates over their lifetime.
ex: Enterprise accounts deliver 8x the LTV of self-serve users.
ex2: Improving onboarding directly increases LTV by reducing early churn.
tip: « EL-TEE-VEE ». Souvent dit « LTV » sans hésitation.
err: LTV brute ≠ LTV en marge ; précisez selon le contexte.
mem: L = Lifetime, T = (the), V = Value.

exp: Total Cost of Ownership — full cost including licenses, operations, training, and migration.
ex: The TCO analysis showed 38% savings versus their on-prem setup.
ex2: Cloud TCO must include egress fees, not just compute.
tip: « TEE-SEE-OH ». Argument clé en vente cloud.
err: TCO inclut les coûts cachés (formation, maintenance), pas juste le prix.
mem: T = Total, C = Cost, O = Ownership.

exp: Return on Investment — what the buyer gets back versus what they spend.
ex: We need to demonstrate clear ROI within the first six months.
ex2: The business case shows 4x ROI over a three-year horizon.
err: « What's the ROI? » est plus naturel que « What ROI? ».
mem: R = Return, O = On, I = Investment.

exp: Software-as-a-Service — software delivered via subscription in the cloud.
ex: Moving to a SaaS model eliminated all infrastructure overhead.
ex2: Most modern SaaS companies follow a product-led growth motion.
tip: Une syllabe, comme « sass ». Évitez « SA-AS ».
err: « A SaaS » est OK ; « SaaSes » au pluriel est argotique.
mem: S-a-a-S : Software-as-a-Service.

exp: Platform-as-a-Service — managed dev platform (runtime, DB, deploy).
ex: Our PaaS lets developers ship features without managing servers.
ex2: Heroku and Vercel are textbook PaaS examples.
err: PaaS ≠ IaaS : PaaS gère le runtime, pas seulement l'infra.
mem: P comme Platform.

exp: Infrastructure-as-a-Service — raw compute, storage, networking.
ex: IaaS gives full flexibility but more operational responsibility.
ex2: AWS EC2 and Azure Virtual Machines are core IaaS offerings.
err: Avec IaaS, le client gère encore l'OS et les patches.
mem: I comme Infrastructure (la fondation).

exp: Built specifically for the cloud, not migrated from legacy systems.
ex: Their cloud-native architecture deploys 50 times a day with zero downtime.
ex2: Cloud-native apps rely on containers, microservices, and CI/CD.
tip: « klaoud NEY-tiv ». Liaison naturelle entre les deux mots.
err: Migrer une app legacy ne la rend pas cloud-native automatiquement.
mem: Né (native) dans le cloud, pas adopté.

exp: Using more than one public cloud provider on purpose.
ex: A multi-cloud strategy prevents vendor lock-in and improves resilience.
ex2: Finance teams often go multi-cloud to negotiate better discounts.
tip: « MUL-ti klaoud ». 'i' bref, comme dans « happy ».
err: Multi-cloud ≠ hybrid cloud (qui inclut l'on-prem).
mem: Multi = plusieurs clouds publics.

exp: A mix of public cloud and on-premises infrastructure.
ex: Their hybrid cloud setup keeps sensitive data on-prem and bursts to public cloud.
ex2: Hybrid cloud is common in regulated industries like banking and healthcare.
tip: « HAÏ-brid klaoud ». Ne dites pas « i-brid ».
err: Hybrid ≠ Multi-cloud : hybrid mélange privé et public.
mem: Hybride = deux mondes (privé + public).

exp: The process of moving systems or data from one environment to another.
ex: The cloud migration is scheduled in three waves over six months.
ex2: We'll run an assessment before kicking off the migration project.
err: Verbe : « to migrate », pas « to migration ».
mem: Comme les oiseaux qui migrent vers un nouvel environnement.

exp: Moving workloads to the cloud as-is, with little or no refactoring.
ex: A lift-and-shift migration gets you to the cloud fast, but you miss most cost benefits.
ex2: Start with lift-and-shift, then refactor critical apps later.
err: Cette approche n'utilise pas les services cloud natifs.
mem: Tu soulèves (lift) et tu déplaces (shift), sans changer.

exp: An application or set of services consuming compute resources.
ex: Which workloads are you planning to move first?
ex2: Mission-critical workloads need multi-region failover.
err: Workload = un système entier, pas juste une tâche.
mem: Work + load = la charge de travail à faire tourner.

exp: The ability to handle more load by adding resources.
ex: Scalability is non-negotiable for Black Friday traffic.
ex2: Horizontal scalability beats vertical scalability for modern web apps.
err: « Scalable » (adj) ≠ « scalability » (nom). Ne pas mélanger.
mem: Comme une échelle (scale) : tu rajoutes des barreaux.

exp: The ability to automatically grow and shrink resources on demand.
ex: Cloud elasticity means you only pay for what you actually use.
ex2: Black Friday is the perfect test of true elasticity.
err: Elasticity ≠ scalability : elasticity descend aussi quand la charge baisse.
mem: Un élastique : ça monte ET ça redescend.

exp: A short trial to validate a solution before buying.
ex: We're running a 30-day PoC against three critical use cases.
ex2: Define exit criteria before kicking off the PoC.
tip: « proof of KON-sept ». À l'oral, dites souvent « P-O-C » lettre par lettre.
err: Pas de PoC sans critères de succès écrits — sinon il s'éternise.
mem: PROUVER que le concept marche avant de signer.

exp: Request for Proposal — formal document asking vendors to bid.
ex: We just received a competitive RFP from a Fortune 500 buyer.
ex2: Bid/no-bid decisions should happen within 48 hours of receiving an RFP.
err: RFI (information) précède souvent l'RFP (proposal).
mem: R = Request, F = For, P = Proposal.

exp: Service Level Agreement — a promise on uptime, response time, etc.
ex: Our SLA guarantees 99.99% uptime for enterprise customers.
ex2: SLA breaches trigger automatic service credits, not refunds.
err: SLA ≠ SLO : SLO est l'objectif interne, SLA l'engagement contractuel.
mem: S = Service, L = Level, A = Agreement.

exp: The first qualifying call where you learn the prospect's pain points.
ex: The discovery call uncovered three urgent business priorities.
ex2: A good discovery call is 80% listening and 20% talking.
err: Évitez de pitcher pendant la discovery : posez des questions.
mem: Découvrir (discover) avant de proposer.

exp: An internal advocate who actively supports your solution inside their company.
ex: Sarah is our champion — she's presenting the business case to the board.
ex2: No enterprise deal closes without a clearly identified champion.
tip: « TCHAM-pi-en ». Le 'ch' = « tch » comme dans « chat (animal) ».
err: Un champion n'est pas forcément le décideur final.
mem: Le champion porte vos couleurs en interne.

exp: Anyone with an interest or influence in the buying decision.
ex: Map every stakeholder before sending the final proposal.
ex2: Misalignment between stakeholders is the number-one reason deals stall.
err: « Stakeholders » au pluriel sans 's' supplémentaire.
mem: Stake (enjeu) + holder (détenteur) = celui qui a un enjeu.

exp: A senior leader who supports the deal or initiative internally at executive level.
ex: Getting the CTO as executive sponsor accelerated the deal by two months.
ex2: Without an exec sponsor, large deals tend to slip every quarter.
err: Sponsor ne signifie pas « décideur final » — c'est un protecteur senior.
mem: Un parrain (sponsor) en haut de la hiérarchie.

exp: Quarterly Business Review — a meeting to review value delivered and align on next steps.
ex: The QBR is your chance to showcase ROI and unlock the next expansion.
ex2: Always co-build the QBR agenda with your champion.
err: QBR sans données mesurées = perte de temps pour le client.
mem: Q = Quarterly, B = Business, R = Review.

exp: The process of getting a new customer set up and successful.
ex: A smooth onboarding reduces time-to-value by 40%.
ex2: Our 30-60-90 onboarding plan covers setup, adoption, and value review.
err: Onboarding ≠ implementation : l'un est humain, l'autre technique.
mem: On + boarding = monter à bord du produit.

exp: How deeply and widely customers actually use the product.
ex: Low adoption is an early warning sign of churn.
ex2: We track adoption at the user, team, and feature level.
err: Logins ≠ adoption. Mesurez des actions à valeur métier.
mem: Adopter le produit comme un nouveau membre de l'équipe.

exp: A composite metric showing how likely a customer is to renew.
ex: The account's health score dropped to red after the main champion left.
ex2: Build the health score from usage, NPS, support tickets, and sentiment.
tip: « helth skor ». Le 'th' est sourd, comme « think ».
err: Un score basé sur un seul signal = score trompeur.
mem: Comme un check-up médical du compte.

exp: A shared roadmap of milestones to reach the customer's business outcomes.
ex: We co-built a success plan with quarterly business milestones.
ex2: A success plan should always tie back to the customer's KPIs.
err: Pas un plan interne caché — il se co-construit avec le client.
mem: Le plan partagé pour atteindre le succès ensemble.

exp: How long it takes a customer to get the first measurable value from the product.
ex: Reducing time-to-value from 60 to 21 days cut early churn by half.
ex2: Onboarding teams obsess over time-to-value.
err: Le TTV se mesure côté client, pas côté setup interne.
mem: Compte à rebours jusqu'au premier vrai gain.

exp: Start with a small contract, then grow it inside the same account.
ex: We landed with one team of 20 users and expanded to 1,200 in 18 months.
ex2: A land-and-expand motion only works if onboarding creates early value.
err: Sans plan de réussite, le « land » devient un mini-deal isolé.
mem: Atterrir d'abord, puis étendre le territoire.

exp: Untapped expansion opportunities within an existing account.
ex: There's significant white space in their European subsidiaries.
ex2: White space mapping happens in every account planning session.
tip: « WAÏT-spéice ». Deux mots en sales/account planning.
err: White space ≠ pipeline : c'est du potentiel, pas du engagé.
mem: L'espace blanc sur la carte du compte, à colorier.

exp: Identifying every relevant person inside a target account and their relationships.
ex: Account mapping revealed three new buying centers we hadn't touched.
ex2: A good account map shows roles, influence, and political dynamics.
err: Sans titres ET sans liens d'influence, ce n'est pas un account map utile.
mem: Une carte du compte, comme une carte d'état-major.

exp: The person with formal authority to approve the purchase.
ex: Who is the ultimate decision maker on this purchase?
ex2: Enterprise deals typically have multiple decision makers.
err: Le « décideur déclaré » n'est pas toujours le vrai décideur.
mem: Celui qui prend (make) la décision (decision).

exp: The person who controls the budget and can approve the purchase.
ex: The CFO is the economic buyer — we need her aligned before pricing.
ex2: Get to the economic buyer early, or the deal will stall in the finance review.
err: L'économique n'est pas forcément l'utilisateur final.
mem: Celui qui tient le porte-monnaie.

exp: Sales qualification framework: Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion.
ex: MEDDIC helps us decide which deals deserve our time.
ex2: Run every late-stage opportunity through MEDDIC weekly.
err: MEDDIC n'est pas un pitch, c'est un filtre de qualification.
mem: Six lettres pour six points de qualification.

exp: Older qualification framework: Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline.
ex: BANT is fast but often too shallow for complex enterprise deals.
ex2: For SMB inbound, BANT is still a useful starting point.
tip: « bant », une syllabe. Le 'a' court comme « cat ».
err: BANT seul ne suffit pas pour les deals enterprise complexes.
mem: B-A-N-T : 4 boîtes à cocher rapides.

exp: A written document quantifying ROI, costs, and risks of buying.
ex: The business case must show both hard savings and revenue impact.
ex2: Procurement won't approve anything without an approved business case.
err: Un slide générique n'est pas un business case ; il faut des chiffres clients.
mem: Le « dossier » qui justifie la dépense.

exp: Application Programming Interface — how two software systems talk to each other.
ex: Our API integrates with any modern CRM in under 30 minutes.
ex2: Public APIs are a powerful land-and-expand wedge.
err: « An API » est correct ; « a API » est faux à l'oral.
mem: A = Application, P = Programming, I = Interface.

exp: A culture and set of practices combining Dev (build) and Ops (run).
ex: Their DevOps maturity means we'll go live faster than the average customer.
ex2: True DevOps requires automation, monitoring, and a blameless culture.
err: DevOps n'est pas un outil — c'est une culture + des pratiques.
mem: Dev + Ops : on casse le mur entre les deux équipes.

exp: Open-source platform to deploy, scale, and manage containers.
ex: Their Kubernetes setup runs 12,000 pods across three regions.
ex2: Kubernetes is the de facto standard for orchestrating containers.
tip: « kou-ber-NÉ-tiz ». Souvent abrégé en K8s : « K-eights ».
err: K8s = Kubernetes (le 8 remplace 'ubernete').
mem: Pilote de conteneurs (κυβερνήτης en grec = pilote).

exp: Cloud model where you run code without managing servers.
ex: Serverless functions cost almost nothing when idle.
ex2: Pricing is per execution and per millisecond of compute used.
err: Les serveurs existent toujours — le client ne les gère juste pas.
mem: Sans (less) serveur visible pour toi.

exp: An architecture splitting an app into small, independent services.
ex: Their microservices architecture makes third-party integrations far easier.
ex2: Microservices increase deployment freedom but add operational complexity.
err: Microservices ≠ monolithe découpé en modules — chacun est déployable seul.
mem: Micro = petit, autonome.

exp: The act of releasing software or infrastructure into a target environment.
ex: The production deployment is scheduled for next Monday night.
ex2: Blue-green deployments reduce downtime to near zero.
err: Deployment ≠ release : tu peux déployer sans activer la feature.
mem: On déploie comme un parachute : doucement et en sécurité.

exp: Large Language Model — an AI model trained on massive text data.
ex: The LLM powers their internal knowledge search.
ex2: Choosing the right LLM balances quality, latency, and cost per token.
err: GPT, Claude, Gemini ne sont pas des concepts mais des LLMs spécifiques.
mem: L = Large, L = Language, M = Model.

exp: Generative AI — AI that creates new content (text, image, code, audio).
ex: GenAI is reshaping how marketing teams produce content at scale.
ex2: Most GenAI deals start with a single high-impact use case.
err: GenAI ≠ AI traditionnel (classification/prédiction).
mem: Gen comme « générer » du contenu original.

exp: Retrieval-Augmented Generation — an LLM grounded with private or company-specific data.
ex: RAG lets the model answer using the customer's proprietary documents.
ex2: RAG can reduce hallucinations on company-specific questions.
err: RAG ≠ fine-tuning : RAG injecte du contexte, fine-tuning ré-entraîne.
mem: R = Retrieval, A = Augmented, G = Generation.

exp: Further training a base model on domain-specific examples.
ex: Fine-tuning on their support tickets boosted accuracy by 31%.
ex2: Start with prompting, then RAG, then fine-tuning only if needed.
tip: US: « faïn TOO-ning ». UK: on entend aussi « TIOU-ning ».
err: Fine-tuning n'efface pas les biais du modèle de base.
mem: Comme accorder (tune) un instrument déjà fabriqué.

exp: Running a trained model to produce a prediction or output.
ex: Inference costs scale with traffic, not with model size at training.
ex2: Caching common inference calls reduces cost by 40%.
err: Inference ≠ training : training crée le modèle, inference l'utilise.
mem: Le modèle infère une réponse en temps réel.

exp: When an AI confidently generates false or fabricated information.
ex: We use guardrails to minimize hallucinations in production.
ex2: Hallucinations are the number-one blocker for GenAI in regulated industries.
err: Halluciner ≠ se tromper : le modèle invente avec assurance.
mem: Comme rêver éveillé : le modèle voit des choses qui n'existent pas.

exp: A unit of text (subword) processed by an LLM. Pricing is per token.
ex: Pricing is based on the number of tokens processed per month.
ex2: Long context windows let you process millions of tokens in one call.
err: 1 token ≠ 1 mot : ~4 caractères en anglais.
mem: Un jeton de métro = une unité élémentaire de transit.

exp: Crafting instructions to get better outputs from a language model.
ex: Good prompt engineering doubled the accuracy of our agent.
ex2: System prompts, few-shot examples, and clear evaluation criteria are core techniques.
err: Un bon prompt > un meilleur modèle, sur de nombreux cas d'usage.
mem: Engineering = on conçoit le prompt comme un produit.

exp: An autonomous AI system that plans actions and uses tools to reach a goal.
ex: The AI agent handles Tier 1 customer support tickets autonomously.
ex2: Agentic workflows are becoming common in support and operations teams.
err: Un chatbot scripté n'est pas un agent : il n'a ni outils ni plan.
mem: Un agent qui agit, pas juste qui répond.

exp: A large general-purpose model that you build other applications on top of.
ex: Choosing the right foundation model balances cost, quality, and speed.
ex2: GPT-4, Claude, and Llama 3 are common foundation models.
err: Foundation model ≠ application : c'est le moteur, pas la voiture.
mem: La fondation sur laquelle on construit ses applis.

exp: Using digital tech to fundamentally change how a business operates.
ex: Cloud adoption is at the core of their digital transformation roadmap.
ex2: Digital transformation fails without strong executive sponsorship.
err: Acheter un outil SaaS ≠ transformation digitale.
mem: Pas juste de l'IT : on transforme tout l'opérationnel.

exp: When switching to another vendor is too costly or difficult.
ex: Our open-standards approach prevents vendor lock-in.
ex2: Procurement always asks about vendor lock-in during negotiation.
err: Tout SaaS crée un certain lock-in ; il faut le minimiser.
mem: Tu te retrouves « verrouillé » chez le fournisseur.

exp: A trial focused on proving business value, not just technical fit.
ex: The PoV showed 200K in projected annual savings.
ex2: In some enterprise sales cycles, a PoV is more useful than a purely technical PoC.
err: PoV = mesure de valeur business, pas une démo technique.
mem: PROUVER la valeur, pas juste la faisabilité.

exp: The skill of acknowledging and addressing buyer concerns.
ex: Objection handling is one of the most critical skills for an AE.
ex2: The best reps ask follow-up questions before responding to objections.
err: Ne contournez pas l'objection : reconnaissez-la d'abord.
mem: Gérer (handle) plutôt que combattre les objections.

exp: The discussion to reach agreement on price, terms, and scope.
ex: Price negotiation should start only after value is fully established.
ex2: Strong negotiators trade concessions, they don't give them away.
err: Verbe : « to negotiate » (pas « to negotiation »).
mem: Discuter pour arriver à un accord.

exp: A formal document presenting price, scope, and terms.
ex: The proposal includes three pricing tiers tailored to their needs.
ex2: Send the proposal as a PDF unless procurement asks for an editable version.
err: « Proposition » en anglais a un autre sens (souvent business value, pas devis).
mem: Ce que tu PROPOSES officiellement au client.

exp: Master Service Agreement — the umbrella contract governing terms for future orders or SOWs.
ex: The MSA will govern every future purchase from this account.
ex2: Once the MSA is signed, future deals only need a short SOW.
err: MSA seul ne génère pas de revenu — il faut un SOW ou Order Form.
mem: M = Master (le contrat-parapluie).

exp: Statement of Work — what exactly will be delivered, when, and for how much.
ex: The SOW details the implementation scope and project timeline.
ex2: Every SOW must reference the parent MSA.
err: Scope flou = SOW flou = projet qui dérape.
mem: S = Statement, O = Of, W = Work.

exp: Non-Disclosure Agreement — keeps shared information confidential.
ex: Sign the NDA before sharing any roadmap details.
ex2: Mutual NDAs protect both parties, not just one.
err: Signer un NDA ≠ être engagé contractuellement à acheter.
mem: N = Non, D = Disclosure, A = Agreement.

exp: Adhering to laws, regulations, and standards (GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001).
ex: GDPR compliance is a blocking requirement for every European customer.
ex2: Compliance reviews can add 6 to 12 weeks to enterprise sales cycles.
err: Compliance ≠ security : la conformité prouve la sécurité par documentation.
mem: On se conforme aux règles externes.

exp: The principle that data is subject to the laws of the place where it is stored or processed.
ex: Data residency requirements can prevent storing personal data outside the EU.
ex2: Choosing an EU region is now table stakes for French public sector deals.
err: Data residency (où ça vit) ≠ sovereignty (quelles lois s'appliquent).
mem: La donnée appartient au territoire où elle réside.

exp: The moment the product is live and used by end users in production.
ex: Go-live is confirmed for the first of next month.
ex2: Plan a post-go-live hypercare window for 30 days.
err: « Live » prononcé /lɪv/ = verbe ; ici on dit /laɪv/.
mem: On passe en LIVE, en direct.

exp: Net Promoter Score — likelihood that customers would recommend you (-100 to +100).
ex: NPS is strongly correlated with renewal and expansion.
ex2: A B2B SaaS NPS above 40 is considered excellent.
err: NPS = promoteurs - détracteurs ; les passifs ne comptent pas.
mem: N = Net, P = Promoter, S = Score.

exp: A specific business problem your product solves.
ex: Their primary use case is automating invoice approvals.
ex2: Anchoring a demo around one strong use case beats showing every feature.
err: Use case ≠ feature : un use case résout un problème métier.
mem: Un usage concret du produit.

exp: A specific, urgent business problem the buyer wants to fix.
ex: Cost control is their most pressing pain point right now.
ex2: No pain, no deal — surface and quantify the pain in discovery.
err: « Pain » signifie « douleur » ici ; rien à voir avec le pain à manger.
mem: Le point où ça fait mal au client.

exp: A clear statement of why a customer should choose you.
ex: Our value proposition centers on speed, security, and measurable savings.
ex2: If the value prop is weak, the forecast will keep slipping.
err: Une fonctionnalité n'est pas une proposition de valeur.
mem: La valeur que tu proposes, en une phrase.

exp: How many times your pipeline exceeds your quota.
ex: We need 3x pipeline coverage to confidently hit our number.
ex2: Below 2.5x coverage, the quarter is already at risk.
err: 3x coverage avec un mauvais pipeline = faux sentiment de sécurité.
mem: Combien de fois ton pipe couvre ton quota.

exp: A mutual document listing all remaining steps to sign by a target date.
ex: A mutual close plan aligns both sides on remaining steps.
ex2: Without a close plan, the deal is likely to slip.
err: « Close » prononcé /kloʊs/ = adjectif (proche), pas la même chose.
mem: Le plan pour fermer (close) le deal proprement.

exp: Reaching out to prospects with no prior relationship.
ex: Cold outreach on LinkedIn generated 15 qualified discovery calls.
ex2: Personalized cold outreach beats high-volume blasts every time.
err: « Cold call » est spécifiquement par téléphone ; outreach inclut email + social.
mem: Sans relation préalable = à froid.

exp: Being introduced to a prospect by someone they already trust.
ex: A warm intro doubled our response rate compared to cold outreach.
ex2: Ask happy customers for warm introductions to their peers.
err: « Warm intro » est plus naturel à l'oral que « warm introduction ».
mem: Le tiers fait le pont, l'ambiance est chaude.

exp: Services where the provider operates the infrastructure on your behalf.
ex: Managed services free the client from day-to-day operations.
ex2: Managed services typically come with premium SLAs.
tip: « MA-nidjd SEUR-vis-iz ». Le 'ed' final est sourd.
err: Managed ≠ self-managed : le client ne gère plus rien d'opérationnel.
mem: On te gère ça pour toi.

exp: Pricing model where you pay for what you actually use.
ex: Consumption-based pricing lowers the barrier to entry for new customers.
ex2: Snowflake popularized consumption pricing in the data space.
err: Consumption ≠ flat subscription : la facture peut varier chaque mois.
mem: Tu paies ce que tu CONSOMMES.

exp: Ensuring customers reach their desired business outcomes with your product.
ex: Customer success is about outcomes, not just satisfaction.
ex2: CS teams own renewal, adoption, and expansion in most modern SaaS companies.
err: CS ≠ support : le support résout des tickets ; CS pilote la valeur.
mem: Ton succès = mon succès.

exp: To briefly reconnect with someone to check in.
ex: I'll touch base with you next week to align before the QBR.
ex2: Let's touch base on Monday to review the action items.
tip: « teutch béice ». Le son /ʌ/ de touch est court, comme dans « cup ».
err: Pas « touch the base » : l'expression est sans article.
mem: Toucher la base (baseball) = revenir au point de départ.

exp: A message or meeting after an initial conversation to keep things moving.
ex: I'll send a follow-up email by end of day with the recap and next steps.
ex2: Most deals are won in the follow-up, not in the first meeting.
err: Verbe : « to follow up » (deux mots) ; nom : « follow-up » (avec tiret).
mem: Tu suis (follow) après (up) la première interaction.

exp: A high-level plan of upcoming features and milestones.
ex: Sharing the product roadmap built trust with the technical buyer.
ex2: Never commit roadmap dates to a customer without product sign-off.
tip: « ROUD-map ». Un seul mot, accent sur ROUD.
err: Un roadmap = direction, pas une promesse contractuelle.
mem: La carte de la route à venir.

exp: The full sequence of stages a customer goes through with your brand.
ex: We mapped the customer journey from first touch to expansion.
ex2: Every churn signal sits somewhere in the customer journey.
err: Customer journey ≠ sales funnel : le journey couvre post-vente aussi.
mem: Le voyage complet de ton client.

exp: Measurable results that matter to the customer's business.
ex: Every meeting must tie back to the customer's business outcomes.
ex2: Activity metrics only matter when they connect to business outcomes.
err: Logins, MAUs, et features sont des outputs — pas des outcomes.
mem: Le résultat (outcome) côté business, pas côté produit.

exp: A product that uses AI as a core component of its features.
ex: Their AI-powered assistant cuts support resolution time in half.
ex2: Buyers are skeptical of AI-powered claims without proof — show the outcome.
err: « AI-powered » est devenu vague : précisez quel modèle, quelle valeur.
mem: Le moteur (power) du produit est de l'IA.

exp: Able to grow to handle more demand without breaking.
ex: Our solution is scalable from 10 to 100,000 users without re-architecting.
ex2: Scalability claims without proof are a red flag in technical reviews.
err: « Scalable » est un adjectif ; « scalability » est le nom associé.
mem: Capable de monter l'échelle (scale).

exp: Keeping customers or users instead of losing them.
ex: Retention is the single biggest driver of long-term SaaS growth.
ex2: Gross retention removes upsell; net retention includes it.
err: Retention ≠ engagement : on peut être engagé mais churner.
mem: Garder (retain) les clients.

exp: Active support and approval from all key people for a project.
ex: Without stakeholder buy-in, the rollout will stall in week two.
ex2: Securing buy-in from finance and IT is the toughest part of enterprise sales.
err: Un email d'accord ≠ vrai buy-in ; il faut un engagement actif.
mem: Acheter (buy) l'adhésion des parties prenantes.

exp: To finalize and sign a sales agreement.
ex: We closed the deal last Friday after a three-month cycle.
ex2: You close deals by helping customers buy, not by pushing harder.
tip: « kloze a dil ». 'close' (verbe) avec /z/ final, pas /s/.
err: « Close » /kloʊs/ (adj) = proche ; « close » /kloʊz/ (verbe) = fermer.
mem: On ferme (close) la boucle commerciale.

exp: To proactively contact someone, especially by email or message.
ex: I'll reach out to the CFO this week to set up an intro call.
ex2: Reach out to me if you have any questions before the demo.
err: Au passé : « I reached out », pas « I reach-outed ».
mem: Tendre la main (reach) vers quelqu'un.

exp: To include someone in a conversation or email thread.
ex: Let me loop in our CS team so they can take it from here.
ex2: Always loop in Legal before sending a redlined contract back.
err: « Loop in » prend un complément (someone) : « loop me in ».
mem: Ajouter quelqu'un dans la boucle de discussion.

exp: To return to a topic or person later with an update or answer.
ex: Let me circle back with the answer once I've checked with Product.
ex2: I'll circle back on pricing after the procurement review.
err: Souvent surutilisé en réunion — préférez « I'll get back to you » par écrit.
mem: Faire un cercle et revenir.

exp: When a deal expected to close in the current period moves to the next.
ex: Three deals are slipping into next quarter — we need a recovery plan.
ex2: Deals slip when there's no close plan or no executive sponsor.
err: « Slipping » ≠ perdu : le deal n'est pas mort, il est en retard.
mem: Le deal glisse hors du trimestre.

exp: Very large in amount, scale or impact — used positively by execs and in sales pitches.
ex: There's tremendous upside if we land just two of these enterprise accounts.
ex2: The team has made tremendous progress on the onboarding flow this quarter.
tip: « tri-MEN-deuss ». Stress sur MEN. Évitez « tré-MAN-douss » à la française.
err: Évitez « very tremendous » : le mot est déjà superlatif.
mem: Tremendous → tremblement → impact qui fait trembler.

exp: Strong, well-built, able to handle real-world load or pushback.
ex: We need a more robust pipeline before we forecast the quarter.
ex2: Their API is robust enough to handle our enterprise volumes.
tip: « roh-BUSST ». Stress sur la 2e syllabe, pas « RO-buste ».
err: « Robust » se prononce avec stress final en anglais, contrairement au français « robuste ».
mem: Pensez à un robot bien bâti : ro-BUST.

exp: Smooth and uninterrupted, especially across systems or steps.
ex: The SSO integration makes the login flow completely seamless for end users.
ex2: We want a seamless handoff from Sales to Customer Success.
err: « Seamless » décrit l'expérience, pas la difficulté du build derrière.
mem: Sans couture (seam = couture) = fluide.

exp: Strong enough to grab attention and drive action — typically about a pitch, case or story.
ex: We need a more compelling business case before we go to the CFO.
ex2: Her demo was compelling — the CTO leaned in within the first 90 seconds.
err: « Compelling reason » est presque un cliché : variez avec « strong rationale ».
mem: Compelling → ça vous pousse (compel) à agir.

exp: At a fine level of detail — often about data, reporting or permissions.
ex: Can you give me a more granular breakdown of churn by segment?
ex2: The dashboard lets you drill down to granular activity at the user level.
err: « Granular » s'applique aux données, pas aux personnes (« a granular person » ✗).
mem: Comme du sable : beaucoup de petits grains de détail.

exp: Specific enough that someone can actually do something with it — about insights, feedback or next steps.
ex: That feedback is interesting but not actionable — what should we change?
ex2: Every QBR should end with three actionable next steps and owners.
err: « Actionable insight » est devenu cliché : préférez « insight we can act on ».
mem: Action + able = sur lequel on peut agir.

exp: By a meaningful amount — used to qualify a measurable change.
ex: Activation rates improved significantly after we shipped the new onboarding.
ex2: Pipeline coverage is significantly below where we need to be for Q4.
err: Ne dites pas « significantly » pour « importantly » : ça parle d'ampleur, pas d'importance.
mem: Significant → grosse différence chiffrée.

fr: En fin de compte / Au final
exp: In the end, after everything is considered — used to bring a discussion to its core point.
ex: Ultimately, the question is whether we have product-market fit in this segment.
ex2: We tested three pricing models, but ultimately the per-seat model won.
tip: « UL-teu-meut-li ». 4 syllabes, 'u' court comme dans « cup ».
syn: at the end of the day
err: « Ultimately » ≠ « finally » (= dernier dans une liste).
mem: Ultimate → le point ultime du raisonnement.

exp: Before being asked — anticipating an issue or need.
ex: Let's proactively reach out to the top 20 accounts before renewal season.
ex2: She proactively flagged the security gap before the audit.
err: Évitez d'en abuser dans les emails — « proactively » sonne corporate.
mem: Pro = avant + active = agir.

exp: In a way that's aligned with broader long-term goals.
ex: We need to strategically pick which segments we double down on next year.
ex2: This hire is strategically important — they own our new EMEA motion.
err: « Strategic » est sur-utilisé : si tout est « strategic », rien ne l'est.
mem: Strategy → comme aux échecs, chaque coup compte.

exp: Used to introduce a brief summary at the end of a discussion or pitch.
ex: To sum up: we ship the beta in May, GA in July, with three pilot customers committed.
ex2: To sum up, the data points to a pricing problem, not a positioning problem.
tip: « teu SOM op ». 'u' court, comme dans « sun ».
err: « To sum up » prend rarement un complément direct — c'est une transition, pas un verbe à objet.
mem: Add things up → sum → résumé.

en: At the end of the day
fr: En fin de compte / Au final
exp: Used to bring a discussion back to its core point, ignoring secondary details.
ex: At the end of the day, the customer just wants a faster time-to-value.
ex2: At the end of the day, we either hit the number or we don't.
tip: « att thi end ov theu DEY ». Liaison fluide.
syn: when all is said and done
err: Surutilisé en réunion — alternez avec « ultimately » ou « bottom line ».
mem: À la fin de la journée, ce qui compte vraiment.

fr: Faire bouger les choses / Avoir un vrai impact
exp: To produce a noticeable, measurable change on a key metric.
ex: Will this feature actually move the needle on activation, or is it just a nice-to-have?
ex2: Cutting onboarding from 14 days to 3 really moved the needle on NRR.
tip: « mouv theu NII-deul ». Le 'd' est presque un 't' doux en anglais US.
err: Si le résultat est faible, dites « doesn't really move the needle ».
mem: L'aiguille (needle) d'un cadran qui bouge → impact mesurable.

exp: An easy win — something quick to do with clear payoff.
ex: Fixing those three onboarding emails is low-hanging fruit — let's ship it this sprint.
ex2: We exhausted the low-hanging fruit; the next wins will take real engineering work.
tip: « lo HANG-ing frout ». Sans accent sur fruit (un seul syllabe).
err: À éviter au pluriel : on dit « low-hanging fruit » (singulier collectif).
mem: Le fruit le plus bas sur l'arbre est le plus facile à cueillir.

exp: To look more closely at a specific subset, especially in data.
ex: Let's drill down into the EMEA numbers — that's where the gap is.
ex2: Can we drill down on why activation drops on day 3?
err: « Drill down on » + sujet ; « drill into » + données.
mem: Comme une perceuse qui creuse dans la donnée.

exp: A detailed, focused exploration of a topic — often a dedicated session.
ex: Let's schedule a deep dive on the pricing model with Finance next week.
ex2: The deep dive surfaced two churn drivers we hadn't seen in the aggregate.
err: « Deep-dive » (verbe) ou « deep dive » (nom) ; en réunion, c'est plus souvent le nom.
mem: Plongée profonde dans un sujet.

exp: To reach shared understanding among stakeholders.
ex: Before we talk to the customer, let's get on the same page internally.
ex2: Sales and Product need to get on the same page about Q3 priorities.
err: « On the same page » ≠ « of the same opinion » : c'est plus large (mêmes faits, mêmes priorités).
mem: Lire le même paragraphe = même compréhension.
alts: etre sur la meme longueur d'onde
être sur la même longueur d'onde

exp: To express disagreement with a decision, request or price.
ex: The buyer pushed back hard on our discount structure.
ex2: It's healthy when engineers push back on unrealistic timelines.
err: « Pushback » (un mot, nom) ≠ « push back » (verbe en deux mots).
mem: Pousser en sens inverse = contester.

exp: To secure agreement and support from key stakeholders before moving forward.
ex: We need to get buy-in from Legal and Security before we can sign.
ex2: Without exec buy-in, this initiative will stall by mid-quarter.
err: « Buy-in » avec trait d'union (nom). « Buy in » sans trait d'union (verbe).
mem: Les gens « achètent » votre idée = adhèrent.

exp: To reach agreement on a specific point or decision.
ex: Can we align on the launch date before we leave this call?
ex2: We aligned on three key metrics for the pilot phase.
err: « Align on » + sujet précis ; « align with » + personne/équipe.
mem: Mettre en ligne = s'accorder.

exp: The time or mental capacity someone has to take on more work.
ex: I don't have the bandwidth to own that project this quarter.
ex2: Do you have bandwidth for a 30-minute discovery call on Thursday?
tip: « BAND-witth ». Le 'dth' final est délicat — un son 'd' suivi de 'th' doux.
err: « Bandwidth » au figuré = capacité humaine, pas la bande passante réseau.
mem: Capacité du tuyau = capacité de la personne.

fr: Dans les détails / Submergé par les détails
exp: Too deep in the details, often at the expense of the big picture.
ex: Let's not get in the weeds on the API spec — we need a yes or no first.
ex2: The exec doesn't want to be in the weeds, just a clear recommendation.
err: « In the weeds » ≠ noyé sous le travail (= « slammed »).
mem: Perdu dans les hautes herbes = perdu dans les détails.

exp: To share a draft or idea with someone to get their input before finalizing.
ex: Let me run it by Legal before we send the redlines back.
ex2: Run the new pricing by your CFO and let me know what they push back on.
err: « Run by » + personne, pas + sujet : « run it by Sarah », pas « run it by pricing ».
mem: Faire passer l'idée DEVANT quelqu'un avant de valider.

fr: En parler à part / Hors réunion
exp: To move a side discussion out of the current meeting to keep the agenda on track.
ex: Great point — let's take it offline so we can finish the agenda.
ex2: We took the contract details offline and closed them by end of day.
err: « Offline » ici n'a rien à voir avec internet : c'est « en dehors de cette réunion ».
mem: Sortir le sujet de la « ligne » de la réunion en cours.

exp: To alert stakeholders to a risk or problem early.
ex: I want to raise a flag on the renewal — the champion just left the company.
ex2: If you see usage drop two weeks in a row, raise a flag with the CSM.
err: « Raise a red flag » insiste sur l'urgence ; « raise a flag » est plus neutre.
mem: Lever un drapeau = signaler un risque visible.

exp: Recognised, noted or formally received — common in business email replies.
ex: Your concern is acknowledged and we'll address it in the next review.
ex2: Receipt of the contract is hereby acknowledged.
tip: « ak-NO-lidjd ». Le 'k' est muet ; stress sur NO.
err: Pas « aknowledged » : il faut le 'c' silencieux.
mem: Ack = signal d'accusé de réception.

exp: Polite invitation to relax or feel comfortable in a situation.
ex: Please be at ease — this is an informal discussion, not an evaluation.
ex2: Be at ease around senior leaders; they want a peer, not a pitch.
err: « At ease » ≠ « easy » : c'est l'état mental, pas la difficulté.
mem: At + ease = en état détendu.

exp: Used to ask someone to remember a point throughout a decision or discussion.
ex: We'll cover three options — bear that in mind when you weigh costs.
ex2: Bear in mind that EMEA pricing must include VAT.
err: « Bear » (porter, ours) ≠ « bare » (nu). Homophones piégeux.
mem: Tu portes (bear) cette pensée dans l'esprit.

exp: To formally grant something — title, honour, privilege — typically by an authority.
ex: The board bestowed the title of Distinguished Engineer on three principals this year.
ex2: Trust is bestowed slowly and lost quickly.
err: « Bestow on/upon someone », pas « bestow to someone ».
mem: Be + stow (ranger) → placer un honneur sur quelqu'un.

exp: Talking with excessive pride about one's achievements — often viewed negatively.
ex: There's a fine line between confidence and boasting in a sales call.
ex2: Without boasting, our retention is the best in the segment.
err: « To boast about » (verbe d'action), pas « to boast on ».
mem: Boast = bombe la poitrine.

exp: To communicate an idea, message or feeling — often more formal than 'tell'.
ex: Please convey our thanks to the security team for the fast response.
ex2: The slide doesn't convey the urgency we want the board to feel.
err: « Convey » s'applique à un message, pas à un objet physique (sauf transport).
mem: Comme un tapis roulant (conveyor) : tu fais passer l'idée.

exp: To desire something strongly, especially something belonging to someone else.
ex: Every account executive on the team covets the Global 2000 patch.
ex2: The CMO role is one of the most coveted positions in the company.
err: Le passé est « coveted », pas « coved ».
mem: Pensé à 'covid'… non, 'co-VIT' — tu en veux à tout prix.

exp: To consider a possibility seriously, without yet committing.
ex: Would you entertain the idea of a multi-year deal with quarterly check-ins?
ex2: The CTO won't even entertain a private-cloud migration this year.
err: Ici « entertain » ≠ divertir. C'est ouvrir l'esprit à une idée.
mem: Recevoir (entertain) une idée comme un invité.

exp: Used to emphasise something surprising or unexpected.
ex: Even our most senior reps struggle with enterprise procurement timelines.
ex2: The model performs well, even on noisy production data.
err: « Even » avant le verbe principal : « we even tested it », pas « we tested it even ».
mem: Mettre l'accent sur quelque chose d'inattendu.

exp: Used to introduce a fact that contrasts with the main clause.
ex: Even though pipeline is healthy, win rates have dropped.
ex2: We shipped on time even though two engineers were out sick.
err: « Even though » + fait réel ; « even if » + hypothèse.
mem: Même + bien que → contraste renforcé.

exp: Used to stress that something is true for a particularly unlikely person — including the speaker.
ex: Even I struggle to remember every clause of the new MSA.
ex2: Even I, after ten years in the space, was surprised by their pricing model.
tip: « II-veun AY ». Bien marquer le AY.
err: « Even me » à l'oral est courant mais moins formel que « even I ».
mem: Même la personne qui parle est concernée.

exp: An impressive achievement, often requiring skill, courage, or effort.
ex: Shipping that platform in six months was no small feat.
ex2: It's a remarkable feat of engineering — three nines of uptime from day one.
tip: « FIIT ». 'ea' = ii long ; ne dites pas 'feet'.
err: « Feat » (exploit) ≠ « feet » (pieds) malgré la prononciation similaire.
mem: Un feat = un exploit dont on parle.

exp: Extremely dirty — also used figuratively for unethical behaviour or huge sums.
ex: That practice is filthy — the regulator would have a field day.
ex2: He made filthy money on that exit and retired at 38.
err: « Filthy rich » est une expression figée signifiant 'immensément riche'.
mem: Filth = saleté → filthy = sale.

exp: Used to add another formal point to an argument, typically in writing.
ex: Furthermore, the new pricing aligns us with the top three competitors.
ex2: The platform is faster; furthermore, it costs 30% less to operate.
tip: « FEUR-theur-mor ». Stress sur la première syllabe.
err: À éviter à l'oral informel — préférez « and » ou « also ».
mem: Va plus loin (further) + en plus (more).

exp: Used in formal writing to add a related and reinforcing point.
ex: The integration cut onboarding time in half; moreover, support tickets dropped 40%.
ex2: Moreover, the new region opens up significant public-sector pipeline.
err: Toujours suivi d'une virgule en début de phrase.
mem: More + over = quelque chose en plus, par-dessus.

exp: To have a good and cooperative relationship with someone.
ex: She's known for getting along with even the toughest procurement teams.
ex2: Getting along with engineering is half the AE's job in technical sales.
err: « Get along with » + personne, pas + tâche.
mem: Avancer ensemble (along) sans friction.

exp: To cause damage — physical, reputational, or commercial.
ex: A public outage would harm the brand far more than a delayed launch.
ex2: This clause could harm us in any future acquisition discussion.
err: « Harm » + objet direct ; pas « harm to someone » sauf en formule (« cause harm to »).
mem: Harm = tort, à éviter à tout prix.

exp: Used to flag that a decision or behaviour produces real negative impact.
ex: Skipping the security review feels efficient but it causes harm downstream.
ex2: It causes harm to morale when feedback never reaches the team.
err: « Cause harm to + someone/something », jamais « cause harm of ».
mem: Ça crée du tort, pas juste de la gêne.

exp: Used to introduce a contrasting statement in a formal tone.
ex: The pilot succeeded; however, the rollout will require additional headcount.
ex2: However tempting the discount, it would break our floor pricing policy.
err: « However » en milieu de phrase prend une virgule de chaque côté.
mem: Un 'mais' poli et formel.

exp: To be unable to grasp or make sense of something, often surprising or absurd.
ex: I can't fathom why they'd walk away from a deal this aligned.
ex2: It's hard to fathom the scale until you see the production traffic.
err: « Fathom » sans 'don't' = saisir. Avec 'can't' = ne pas saisir.
mem: Fathom = unité de profondeur → mesurer la profondeur d'une idée.

exp: To investigate or consider beyond the surface or current scope.
ex: Look further than this quarter — what does the segment look like in 18 months?
ex2: If you want talent like that, you won't have to look further than this team.
err: « Further » pour la métaphore ; « farther » pour la distance physique.
mem: Regarder au-delà de ce qui est évident.

exp: The extent of one's understanding or reach.
ex: That kind of advanced ML architecture is outside my grasp — let's get a SE on the call.
ex2: The fundamentals are now within my grasp after three months of ramp.
err: « Grasp » s'utilise au singulier dans cette expression.
mem: Grasp = saisir → la portée de ta compréhension.

exp: Beyond what one can understand, achieve, or control.
ex: The CTO meeting was out of my grasp this week — we'll loop in the RVP.
ex2: That promotion is still out of my grasp without two more enterprise wins.
err: Reconnaître ce qui est out of grasp est un signe de maturité, pas de faiblesse.
mem: Trop loin pour être attrapé.

exp: Used to transition to a specific topic just mentioned.
ex: On that, let me share what Procurement sent over last night.
ex2: Quick build on that — we saw a similar pattern in EMEA.
err: « On that note » = transition complète ; « on that » = enchaînement court.
mem: Reprendre la balle sur le sujet venant d'être lancé.

exp: Indicates movement towards a position on top of something, or transition to a new topic.
ex: Let's move onto the next quarter's targets.
ex2: She quickly latched onto the strategic implications of the new pricing.
err: « Onto » (mouvement) ≠ « on to » (deux mots, autre construction).
mem: On + to → vers et dessus.

exp: In a different way, or as a consequence of something not happening.
ex: We need exec buy-in by Friday — otherwise the launch slips.
ex2: The deal is solid; otherwise, the forecast would be off by 200K.
err: « Otherwise » au début d'une phrase prend toujours une virgule.
mem: Other + wise → d'une autre manière.

exp: In a careless way, without regard for risk or consequence.
ex: They scaled the team recklessly and now half the desks are empty.
ex2: Don't discount recklessly — it sets a precedent for the next renewal.
err: « Reckless » (adj) ≠ « wreckless » (n'existe pas).
mem: Reck (souci) + less → sans souci du risque.

fr: Quoi qu'il en soit / Malgré tout
exp: Without considering the situation or in spite of it.
ex: Regardless of the cost, we need to protect the brand here.
ex2: The team shipped on time regardless of two unexpected outages.
err: « Irregardless » n'existe pas en anglais standard — utilisez « regardless ».
mem: Sans (less) considération (regard) du contexte.

exp: A feeling of reassurance after pressure, worry or pain.
ex: It was a real relief to see the renewal come in last night.
ex2: The new tooling will be a relief to the support team — current ticket volume is unsustainable.
err: « Relief » (nom) ≠ « relieve » (verbe).
mem: Re + lief (léger) → on se sent plus léger.

exp: Unable to relax or stay still, often due to anxiety or impatience.
ex: The board is getting restless about the EMEA hiring plan.
ex2: Customers grow restless when status updates slip more than once.
err: « Restless » ne signifie pas « fatigué » — c'est l'opposé du repos calme.
mem: Sans (less) repos (rest) → agité.

exp: Showing strong contempt or disrespect toward someone or something.
ex: His tone became scornful the moment we mentioned a competitor's solution.
ex2: Avoid scornful language in objection handling — it always backfires.
err: À éviter dans toute communication client — détruit la confiance.
mem: Scorn = mépris → scornful = qui méprise.

exp: In serious trouble — informal but extremely common in tech and sales.
ex: If we miss this renewal, the Q4 number is screwed.
ex2: We're screwed without exec sponsorship on this account.
err: Informel ; à éviter en client meeting formel, OK entre collègues.
mem: Comme une vis qui a foiré : tout est bloqué.

fr: Plusieurs fois plus / Multiplié par plusieurs
exp: By multiple times the original amount — a formal multiplier.
ex: Inference costs dropped severalfold after we migrated to the new instances.
ex2: The TAM has grown severalfold in the past three years.
err: « Severalfold » en un seul mot. Pas « several-fold » dans la prose pro.
mem: Several + fold → plié plusieurs fois en taille.

exp: Lacking any sense of embarrassment, often about behaviour others might find inappropriate.
ex: It was a shameless pitch — half the slides were about their CEO.
ex2: Shameless plug, but our case study on this exact use case is in the deck.
err: « Shameless plug » est une formule auto-dérisoire courante en présentation.
mem: Shame + less → sans honte.

exp: In a way that is obviously and openly bad or inappropriate.
ex: They so blatantly copied our pricing page — even the typos are the same.
ex2: The clause was so blatantly one-sided that procurement walked away.
err: « Blatant » est négatif : on ne dit pas « blatantly excellent ».
mem: Si visible que personne ne peut l'ignorer.

exp: Surprised, shocked or unsettled — usually by something unexpected.
ex: I was taken aback when they pushed for a 60% discount on day one.
ex2: The CFO was taken aback by the accuracy of our forecasting model.
tip: « TEY-keun eu-BAK ». Stress sur TEY et BAK.
err: Toujours au passif : « I was taken aback », pas « it taken me aback ».
mem: On te tire (take) en arrière (aback) → surprise.

exp: Done with great care, completeness, and attention to detail.
ex: Their security review is the most thorough I've seen this year.
ex2: A thorough discovery saves you from three months of misalignment later.
err: « Thorough » (adj) ≠ « through » (préposition) ≠ « though » (conjonction).
mem: Tu fais le tour complet, en profondeur.

exp: Used to introduce a contrast — softer and more conversational than 'although'.
ex: The numbers look great this quarter, though we shouldn't get complacent.
ex2: Though the budget is tight, the strategic value justifies the spend.
err: « Though » (contraste) ≠ « through » (à travers) ≠ « thought » (pensée).
mem: Petit frère de « although ».

exp: An idea, opinion, or moment of mental activity. Also past tense of 'think'.
ex: My initial thought is to run a smaller pilot before we commit to the full rollout.
ex2: Quick thought before we move on — have we validated this with Legal?
err: « Thought » (nom/passé de think) ≠ « through » ≠ « though ».
mem: Le résultat de penser = pensée.

exp: To suggest a plan, idea or terms for someone to consider.
ex: I'd like to propose a phased rollout starting with the top three regions.
ex2: Let me propose a different framing for the renewal conversation.
tip: « teu preu-POHZ SUM-thing ». Stress sur POHZ.
err: « Propose » + objet direct ; « propose to + someone » = demander en mariage.
mem: Mettre une proposition sur la table.

exp: To ask someone to marry you — the romantic meaning of 'propose'.
ex: He proposed to her last weekend after ten years together.
ex2: Don't say 'I'd like to propose to you' in a sales meeting — say 'I'd like to make a proposal'.
err: En contexte business, dites « make a proposal », jamais « propose to you ».
mem: « To » + personne = romantique.

exp: Anxious or uncomfortable, often about a situation that might go wrong.
ex: I'm uneasy about the close plan — too many things have to land on the same week.
ex2: The team feels uneasy about the new comp model before they see real examples.
err: « Uneasy » s'accorde avec un sentiment, pas avec une chose difficile.
mem: Pas (un) à l'aise (easy) → inquiet.

exp: To release something powerful that was held back — capacity, potential, or impact.
ex: The new pricing will unleash significant pipeline in mid-market.
ex2: Removing those approval steps unleashed the team's velocity.
err: « Unleash » a une charge forte — réservez-le aux changements majeurs.
mem: Détacher la laisse (leash) → libérer.

exp: A formal alternative to 'on', often used for timing or contractual clauses.
ex: Payment is due upon receipt of the signed order form.
ex2: Upon reflection, we should push the launch to Q1.
err: En business writing formel, « upon » remplace souvent « on » pour gagner en gravité.
mem: « Up » + « on » → posé dessus, au moment de.

exp: Used to introduce a choice between two or more possibilities.
ex: We need to decide whether to expand EMEA or double down on North America.
ex2: Whether or not Procurement approves, Legal will still review the clause.
err: « Whether » (choix) ≠ « weather » (météo). Souvent confondu à l'écrit.
mem: Whether → toujours un choix binaire ou multiple.

exp: A vivid example of the 'whether X or not' structure used to dismiss alternatives.
ex: Whether he dies or not, the dynasty was already on its knees.
ex2: In Shakespeare's plays, characters often pose the dilemma: whether to act or not, to live or to die.
err: En contexte pro, préférez « whether the deal closes or not » à des exemples dramatiques.
mem: Whether + verbe + or not → ne change rien à la conclusion.

exp: Used to describe simultaneous actions, or to introduce a contrast.
ex: While Sales focuses on net new, CS will run the expansion plays.
ex2: While the discount is generous, the multi-year commit is what unlocks it.
err: « While » (contraste/simultanéité) ≠ « a while » (un moment).
mem: Deux choses en parallèle, ou en opposition.

exp: Ready and open to do something, often as part of negotiation.
ex: Are you willing to consider a two-year commit in exchange for the discount?
ex2: The CTO is willing to sponsor the pilot if Procurement approves the SOW.
err: « Willing to + base verb » : « willing to consider », pas « willing for considering ».
mem: Avoir la volonté (will) de.

exp: Inside the limits of time, space or an organisation.
ex: We'll deliver the first phase within six weeks of signature.
ex2: Within EMEA, public sector is our fastest-growing segment.
err: « Within » (limite incluse) ≠ « in » (général).
mem: Avec (with) + dedans (in) → à l'intérieur des limites.

exp: To say something repeatedly or without thinking — usually critical.
ex: You spout that line about 'customer obsession' but the data tells a different story.
ex2: Don't just spout buzzwords in interviews — back every claim with a STAR story.
err: « Spout » est péjoratif — implique un discours mécanique ou creux.
mem: Une fontaine qui spout = qui jaillit sans contrôle.

exp: Showing a deep, accurate understanding — often used to praise a comment or analysis.
ex: That was an insightful question about our churn cohorts.
ex2: The post-mortem was the most insightful I've read on this incident class.
err: Évitez d'en abuser dans les compliments — ça devient un tic américain.
mem: In + sight → tu vois à l'intérieur des choses.

exp: The ability to anticipate what will happen and act in advance.
ex: It took real foresight to lock in compute capacity before the AI demand spiked.
ex2: Their hiring plan shows remarkable foresight about the GTM motion.
err: « Foresight » (n.) ≠ « foresee » (v.). On dit « show foresight », pas « foresight something ».
mem: Voir (sight) avant (fore) → prévoyance.

fr: N'a rien donné / Parti à néant
exp: To have come to nothing despite effort — a formal way to say work was wasted.
ex: Six months of negotiation has gone to naught after the merger.
ex2: All those discovery calls have gone to naught — they went with the incumbent.
tip: « haz gonn teu NOTT ». 'au' = o ouvert.
err: « Naught » (zéro littéraire) ≠ « not » (négation).
mem: Naught = zéro → tout est revenu à zéro.

exp: Having no purpose, value or significance.
ex: That metric is meaningless without a baseline.
ex2: Pipeline coverage is meaningless if half the deals aren't qualified.
err: Distinguer « meaningless » (vide de sens) de « insignificant » (peu important).
mem: Meaning + less → sans sens.

exp: Worth the time, effort or cost invested.
ex: The integration project is heavy but absolutely worthwhile for retention.
ex2: Is a 30-minute discovery call worthwhile if the budget isn't confirmed?
err: « Worthwhile » en un seul mot, pas « worth while ».
mem: Worth + while → ça vaut le temps passé.
